newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude to test $20.65 support.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude to test $20.65 support.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
+ NYMEX crude for July has twice tested support at $20.65 and overnight trading set the stage for another test.
+ A break through these levels would indicate a move towards $20.50.
NYMEX crude oil futures have moved sharply lower this week and have twice tested support at $20.65 a barrel. Traders expect another test of this double bottom again.
July NYMEX crude closed unchanged on Wednesday at $20.79 a barrel while June heating oil gained 0.12 cent a gallon to end at 55.39 and June gasoline rose by 0.42 cent to close at 65.80 cents.
"The lows at $20.65 have been support for the past few days and I expect (fundamental news on the physical markets) will see them broken before we go much higher," one Washington-based chartist said.
"If we break that then the next level is around $20.50."
This latter level, he said, lies adjacent to a series of highs from April and early May.
"In general our technical indicators are in a corrective phase - the five-day and the 35-day moving averages are coming together and our stochastics are mid-range but really pointing downwards."

In addition, he said that a move below $20.50 would create an overlap on the Elliott Wave analysis with the fourth wave overlapping the first one. "If that happens then it tells us that it was not one, two, three waves then four - it means some other formation is in place. If it goes further down then the rally really is kaput."

GNI Research in London also sees $20.65 as the first hurdle. "The first downside marker for WTI (crude) is $20.65," the company said in a daily report, adding: "Heating oil is the most vulnerable today."
MeesPierson Derivatives, also in London, said: "The preparation is tending towards the short side and therefore we must look to sell rallies $20.96 or higher."
"Look to buy back initially at $20.64 or on a buying extreme," the report said, using the company's Market Profile chart technique.

The Washington-based chartist said support on the July gasoline chart would be found at 62.00-62.15 cents a gallon. These numbers date from a high on April 30, as well as a double bottom from May 12 and 14 and the low point of May 27.
"If those numbers go then that is history," he said.
MeesPierson said of the June gasoline contract that support would be found first at 65.25 cents and then 64.65, while resistance would weigh in at 66.15, 66.60, and 67.50.
-- Nicholas Shaxson, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8167
